note: The shape of web/data/lyrics.json (made by src/apply_lyrics.py from lyrics_timing.json and your own input/lyrics_lines.txt). The text here is a placeholder, not the song's lyrics. One entry per sung phrase; every character has the second it lands on screen (t) and, when it is sung by itself, the karaoke file's own time (file). A full-width space or a bracket has a t but no file: it arrives with its neighbour.
